claims.text: The personal saving rate was 5.0 percent, with personal saving of $932.3 billion in July.

excerpts.quotation:
Personal saving was $932.3 billion in July and
the personal saving rate—personal saving as a percentage of disposable personal income—was 5.0
percent (table 1).

claims.text: Nominal (current-dollar) spending is distinct from the PCE price index: the price index decreased 0.1 percent in July, meaning the 0.1 percent nominal PCE increase occurred alongside slightly falling prices; real PCE rose 0.2 percent.

excerpts.quotation:
The PCE price index decreased 0.1 percent. Excluding food and energy, the PCE price index increased 0.1
percent (table 9). Real DPI increased 0.3 percent in July and real PCE increased 0.2 percent; goods
increased 0.2 percent and services increased 0.2 percent (tables 5 and 7).

claims.text: Harbor Labs consolidated revenue increased 5 percent.
